headline: Day 1 of Max Edge: Bold Bet on the 76ers over the Pistons at 53.5¢, plus a 3-month buy on T-Mobile at its cheapest valuation in a decade after Friday's SpaceX scare
top_call: Wireless stocks got crushed Friday on a report that SpaceX wants 80,000 U.S. cell sites, but Barron's says T-Mobile has five times SpaceX's spectrum and trades at about 12.5x forward earnings, its lowest in over a decade. Our read: buy TMUS as a 3-month call, graded against the S&P 500.
backdrop: The Dow fell 1.2% (653 points) to 52,215.16 and the S&P 500 0.5% to 7,623.68 Friday as WTI crude settled at $103.27; the Nasdaq slipped 0.2%. This week brings a Fed decision Wednesday plus Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Verizon (Monday) earnings.

finance.label: TMUS
finance.entry_note: Yahoo Finance, Fri Oct 23 close (weekend edition)
finance.why: Barron's: T-Mobile has ~400 MHz of spectrum to SpaceX's 80 and trades at ~12.5x forward earnings, a decade low.
finance.risk: It fell 7.7% Friday; if SpaceX lands cell-site deals faster than Citi's 'years away' estimate, the multiple can compress more.
finance.target_note: Yahoo Finance analyst mean target (25 analysts), Oct 25

right: Postpaid account adds land at or above the ~250,000 T-Mobile guided to
Management says the churn from the rate-plan switch is already easing
The 950,000 to 1.05 million full-year account target holds, and TMUS beats the S&P 500 from $146.54 by late January (that's the actual grade)
wrong: Adds miss the ~250,000 guide and churn keeps climbing
Service revenue comes in under the ~$19.3 billion guide
Talk of SpaceX's spectrum grabs the call and the 'decade-low multiple' just gets lower
catalyst.max: Same night as Microsoft, so Wednesday I find out if I'm a genius twice or wrong in stereo. T-Mobile has beaten EPS 8 quarters straight; the stock just has to stop acting like it hasn't.

ai.headline: Microsoft says China-aligned hackers used the ARTEX agentic AI framework after the ConnectWise breach, hitting 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants at ~2,900 sign-in attempts a minute
ai.why: Some attacks reached privileged cloud access in under three hours; AI agents are now running intrusions at machine speed.

ai.why: Governments are picking AI vendors on security contracts, and the enterprise incumbent is winning that fight.

ai.headline: Anthropic donates Agent Skills to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, as OpenAI, Hugging Face and Alibaba add projects too
ai.why: Skills are already in 70+ agent platforms with ~280M installs; the agent stack's plumbing is going vendor-neutral.

ai.headline: Hugging Face's $399 Microduck robots pass 20,000 preorders after Jensen Huang played with them on stage at GTC Berlin
ai.why: Consumer robots are finding real demand at toy prices, a market Nvidia wants to supply with chips and models.
